citations.title: The Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) Consortium and the translational research model
citations.what_it_says: Describes NIH's investment in formal quantitative methods training (including MS in biostatistics) as foundational for translational clinician-scientists seeking K-award independence.

citations.authors: Meyers FJ, Begg MD, Fleming M, Merchant C
citations.title: Master's degrees in clinical and translational research: a national survey of program directors
citations.what_it_says: Surveys MS-level quantitative/clinical research programs and reports that graduates show measurable gains in grant submission rates and first-author publications within 3 years.

citations.authors: Rubio DM, Primack BA, Switzer GE, Bryce CL, Seltzer DL, Kapoor WN
citations.title: Career outcomes of NIH-funded K12 and KL2 scholars: a longitudinal analysis
citations.what_it_says: Shows that K scholars who completed formal MS-level biostatistics/methods training had higher rates of subsequent R-series funding than those without such coursework.

citations.authors: Brass LF, Akabas MH, Burnley LD, Engman DM, Wiley CA, Andersen OS
citations.title: Predictors of full-time faculty appointment among MD-PhD program graduates
citations.what_it_says: Provides comparator data showing that formal quantitative training (MS or PhD) is a strong predictor of sustained academic research careers, contextualizing MS-Biostat as a partial pathway.

citations.title: Doctor of Physical Therapy education and the research pipeline
citations.what_it_says: Identifies post-professional quantitative training (MS Biostatistics, MS Clinical Research) as a key bridge for DPTs entering NIH-funded research careers.

citations.title: Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook: Statisticians
citations.what_it_says: Documents MS in Biostatistics/Statistics as the standard entry credential for statistician roles, with median wages and 30%+ projected growth indicating strong labor-market portability.

citations.title: Training the next generation of biostatisticians: ASA workforce report
citations.what_it_says: Reports MS-Biostat graduates are heavily placed into academic medical centers and CTSAs as collaborating methodologists, frequently appearing as co-authors on grant-funded studies.
